items.title: Joe Muranyi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: there was a guy named Max Amayer, a booking agent sort of. And he called me a couple of times

ctx.x: Well a break in the night. I knocked around for a while and you know, you get to know people that are similarly inclined, you know, your kind of jazz. And I got to know George Wettling. There was a guy named Dick Webb, the trombone player, he was the editor of Boating magazine. A very nice trombone player and a darling guy, he was the greatest guy in the world, quite a sailor, I used to do a lot of sailing with him. And Dick knew George Wettling and I lived in the Village and George Wettling lived a block or two…

more than $100, it was $150, was with Jimmy McPartland and we had to drive to Cleveland and back. And I went on the road with him too. And the Dixieland and that old tradition, that old time Chicago jazz, it continued in Ohio in Columbus and Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and places like that, they had clubs and the people were still interested in that kind of music. So I got all involved in that and things went along and went along. I played with this one and that one and there was a guy named Max Amayer, a booking…
You were in one of them?
